🍠 When to plant three-leaved yam (bitter yam) in Nigeria

Also called Ẹ̀súrú (Yoruba) and Ona (Igbo).

Quick answer: Plant three-leaved yam (bitter yam) in Nigeria from March to April and harvest from October to December. Planted early in the rains and harvested late in the year.

PlantMarch to April
HarvestOctober to December
Grows inSouth-West and South-East
TypeRoots & tubers
Local namesẸ̀súrú · Ona
JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec

■ plant   ■ harvest

About three-leaved yam (bitter yam)

Ẹ̀súrú yam (Dioscorea dumetorum) hardens soon after harvest, so it must be cooked quickly.

How to plant three-leaved yam (bitter yam) well

Cook within a day or two of harvest; tubers harden in storage.

Planted early in the rains and harvested late in the year.

Diseases and pests of three-leaved yam (bitter yam)

  • Yam anthracnoseUse clean seed and rotate fields.
  • Yam beetlesPlant on time and keep the field clean.

Best states for three-leaved yam (bitter yam)

Ogun · Oyo · Osun · Enugu · Anambra · Imo

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant three-leaved yam (bitter yam) in Nigeria?

Plant three-leaved yam (bitter yam) in Nigeria from March to April and harvest from October to December. Planted early in the rains and harvested late in the year.

What is three-leaved yam (bitter yam) called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Three-leaved yam (Bitter yam) is called Ẹ̀súrú (Yoruba) and Ona (Igbo).

When is three-leaved yam (bitter yam) harvested in Nigeria?

Three-leaved yam (Bitter yam) is usually harvested from October to December.

Which Nigerian states grow the most three-leaved yam (bitter yam)?

Ogun, Oyo, Osun, Enugu, Anambra and Imo are among the best-known three-leaved yam (bitter yam) states.

Can I grow three-leaved yam (bitter yam) in my part of Nigeria?

Three-leaved yam (Bitter yam) grows best in the South-West and South-East regions. In other regions, ask your ADP extension officer before planting.

What diseases attack three-leaved yam (bitter yam) and how do I prevent them?

Yam anthracnose: Use clean seed and rotate fields. Yam beetles: Plant on time and keep the field clean.
